raw_response:
I farm the same 34.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so I will put all 34.1 mu into winter wheat first, then summer maize after harvest. I am not the kind to gamble much at my age. I start from what has worked on our side of Hebei, then I adjust a little by water and price. We have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage and not let the crop sit dry at the key time. For wheat, I will use improved seed and put a solid base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress nitrogen when the seedlings turn and again around jointing if the stand looks hungry. Wheat here can give good grain only if I feed it enough, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives steady ears if the water keeps up. I will keep fertilizer a little heavier on nitrogen for maize, because maize eats strongly, but I will still give phosphorus and potassium so the stalk stays strong and the ear fills better. On this much land, I care about doing the work fast and on time, so I will mostly use rotary tillage after each harvest instead of slow deep ploughing every season. For pesticide, I will not spray blindly, but I will plan on a few times for weeds and insects because once the field gets away from me, the loss is bigger than the spray cost.
